item.title: [OpenWrt-RPi4] 3. Bringing up an SSD1306 in U-Boot on an OpenWrt image for the Raspberry Pi 4
item.description:
Goal

  • Bring up an SSD1306 OLED display over I2C in U-Boot running on the Raspberry Pi 4 (bcm2711).

Now that the Pi 4 boots with U-Boot (previous post ), our job is to add SSD1306 display support to it. We start from how the SSD1306 is brought up in the Linux kernel.

item.title: [Device-Driver-Lichee] 3. Gpioget, controlling an LED with a button
item.description:
I said we would use a button, but I turned my pile of electronics upside down and found no through-hole buttons, only SMD ones. So in this post I use a potentiometer playing the role of a button :vv

item.title: [Device-Driver-Lichee] 1. Build the image and flash it to the board
item.description: Instead of using yocto, which I think is actually quite complicated for beginners, I simplify things by building u-boot and the kernel separately and taking a ready-made root file system to flash to the board. Then we start the Device Driver series without needing to care what yocto is :vv
